hypothesis: Source-preserving: lower temp (0.1), strict verbatim instructions, 2-3 sentence limit. Meeting insight: AI adds extra info vs human data that preserves exact source text. Health domain = one wrong word is dangerous.

Exp2: Keep source-preserving constraint but allow 3-4 sentences and require medication names/dosages/timeframes. Exp1 groundedness=0.96 was great but specificity=0.67 and RAG faithfulness=0.69 need improvement.

Exp3: Revert to Exp1 source-preserving prompt (2-3 sentences), increase QA_PER_SOURCE from 8→12 for 60 pairs total. Coverage bottleneck: Exp1 had 4 questions scoring 0.0 due to missing topics in 40-pair KB.
Exp4: Few-shot prompting with 3 gold-standard human QA examples. Revert to QA_PER_SOURCE=8. Exp1 prompt + examples should improve specificity and tone by showing the model what good pairs look like.
Exp5: Two-pass extraction + temp=0.0. Prompt asks model to first identify key facts from source, THEN compose QA pairs from those facts only. Maximum determinism + explicit grounding step.

Exp6: Keep Exp5 two-pass approach (new best), add adversarial self-check: 'After composing each pair, verify every claim. If any claim cannot be found verbatim in the source, revise or remove it.' Target: boost the 0.5-scoring questions by reducing partial hallucination.

Exp7: Switch to gpt-4o (from gpt-4o-mini) with Exp5 two-pass prompt. Larger model should produce higher quality QA pairs with better semantic coverage and clinical accuracy. Testing model quality vs cost trade-off.

Exp8: Category-aware generation. Require each pair to cover a distinct category (medications, withdrawal, coping, health effects, social, financial, methods, prevention). Should maximize topical diversity within each chunk and improve RAG retrieval coverage for varied test questions.

Exp9: Exp5 two-pass approach but temp=0.2 instead of 0.0. Slight randomness may produce more varied question phrasing, improving semantic diversity in ChromaDB and boosting RAG retrieval hits for diverse test questions.

Exp10: Exp5 two-pass + retrieval-optimized. Ask model to include relevant medical terms and synonyms in answers (e.g., 'nicotine replacement therapy (NRT)' not just 'NRT'). More keyword surface area = better cosine retrieval matches for varied test questions. temp=0.0.
